data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The panel-plus-checklist is genuinely more reliable only if, on the subset of cases where the checklist's rule guidance diverges from the expert's intuitive judgment, the panel follows the checklist and is subsequently verified as correct by the objective outcome at a rate exceeding the expert's base rate.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The divergence stratum is empty, meaning the checklist and expert always agree; in this case, the checklist is trivial and no single-evaluation evidence can distinguish rule-mediated gain from noise reduction.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The panel outperforms the expert on divergent cases but does so by defying the checklist's explicit guidance, indicating the gain is caused by the panel's collective intuition, not the checklist.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Causal mechanism: The checklist encodes explicit, domain-specific decision rules. When these rules conflict with intuition (the divergence stratum), the checklist exerts a causal force on the panel's judgment. If the panel complies and achieves higher accuracy specifically on these cases, the checklist's rule content\u2014not mere procedural compliance or crowd-averaging\u2014is demonstrated to be the operative cause of the reliability gain.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
